section_1.title: Prerequisites: The Circular Motion Foundation
section_1.content: Introduce Euler's formula (e^ix = cosx + isinx) as the building block. Explain that any periodic function can be viewed as the projection of multiple rotating vectors (epicycles) working in harmony.
section_1.example: Visualize a robotic arm drawing a complex shape by combining several simple, constant-speed circular rotations.

section_2.title: Fourier Series: Decomposing the Wave
section_2.content: Define the Fourier series as a 'musical chord' of sine and cosine waves. Explain that any complex periodic signal is just a summation of simple harmonic waves with different frequencies and amplitudes.
section_2.example: Think of a synthesizer: a single complex 'piano' note is actually a collection of pure sine wave frequencies playing together.

section_3.title: Connecting to the Heat Equation
section_3.content: Introduce the 1D heat equation (du/dt = k * d^2u/dx^2). Explain why sine waves are the 'eigenfunctions' of this equation—they keep their shape as they decay, allowing us to solve heat distribution problems by decomposing the initial state into Fourier components.
section_3.example: A metal rod heated in the middle: the heat spreads out like a wave smoothing itself out, calculated by tracking how each Fourier frequency component fades over time.

section_4.title: Visual Synthesis and Application
section_4.content: Show the animation of heat dissipation: An initial jagged temperature spike is decomposed into a set of waves; each wave shrinks exponentially; the sum of these shrunken waves reconstructs the smooth temperature curve over time.
section_4.example: A 'Robot Chef' monitoring the temperature of a pizza slice, using Fourier analysis to predict exactly when the cold spots in the dough will reach the perfect baking temperature.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.2
                y = 2.0 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Connecting to the Heat Equation", [
            "The heat equation describes energy dispersal.",
            "Sine waves remain stable as they decay.",
            "Fourier components solve heat distribution problems."
        ])
        
        # Visuals
        heat_map = Square(side_length=3, fill_opacity=0.6, color=BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color('#FFD700'))

        self.play(Write(laplacian))
        self.play(laplacian.animate.set_color('#FFFF00'))
        self.wait(2)
